column2: req_desc

Health route
The app serves its pages and its JSON interface on one origin and answers `GET /api/health` with 200 and `{"status":"ok"}` once ready.

Stored collections
Records live in PostgreSQL in collections with exactly the names listed in Services, and the constraints listed there hold in the stored data.

Seed data
The app seeds the workspaces, users, pipeline and catalog listed in Seed data once and never duplicates them on restart.

Sessions and lockout
Sign-in returns a bearer token, sign-out invalidates it, and wrong passwords answer 401 and then lock the email, identically for known and unknown emails, as qualified in Business rules.

Closed sign-up
Nobody can create an account except by accepting an admin's invitation.

Viewer is read-only
A viewer reads every workspace record and receives 403 for every create, change, check, run, cancel, reset, Builder read and sample event.

Editor limits
An editor receives 403 from member, plan and audit routes.

Session required
Every console request without a valid session answers 401.

Workspace isolation
A user from another workspace gets 404 for this workspace's records, Builder projects and custom connectors, and no list, count or figure includes them.

Sign-in pages
`/login` signs a person in and opens the address the server returns, shows and announces the wrong-password and locked messages, and "Sign out" returns to the home page.

Request identity
Every `/api` response carries an `X-Request-Id`, every error body repeats it as `request_id`, every request writes one structured stdout log line with it, and a job records the id of the request that started it.

Invitations
An admin invites a person with a role, and the invitation is accepted once, before it expires, with a password of at least twelve characters.

Roles
An admin changes a member's role, and the workspace always keeps at least one admin.

Members and settings pages
The "Invite member" form shows the invite link once and announces its errors, the members list changes roles, and only an admin sees the "Plan" select.

Audit chain
Every audited change enters a gapless hash-chained audit log naming its actor, and no audit event can be changed or deleted.

Catalog interface
The public catalog lists the built-in definitions and filters them by type, category, availability and name.

Catalog page
`/connectors` narrows its cards by search and filters with a politely announced "Showing N" count, keeps the filters in its address, and restores them on reload and on Back.

Sources
Only runnable definitions become sources, source settings are validated, a source check reports rejected credentials and the sample source exposes its three streams.

Secret API key
A source API key is never stored as readable text and never appears in any response, header, check message, job record, log line, live event, audit event or stdout log, refused submissions included.

Sources page
The "New source" form shows a refused value's error beneath its field and creates the source.

Plan limits
The plan sets the minimum schedule interval, an admin changes the plan, and an interval or cron schedule more frequent than the plan allows is refused.

Connection creation
A valid connection is stored active at version 1 with a name unique in the workspace and warehouse tables no other connection to that destination targets.

Connection validation
An invalid stream, sync mode, cursor, prefix, cron expression or time zone is refused with field errors and nothing stored.

Next run
`next_run_at` follows the manual, interval and cron rules, cron matching wall-clock minutes in the connection's time zone across DST changes.

Connection wizard
The four-step wizard keeps values on "Back", shows the schedule fields for the chosen schedule, including "Time zone" for Cron only, and creates the connection.

Connections dashboard
`/app` shows the health cards, the monitor line and the connection list with a "New connection" button.

Full refresh sync
A succeeded full refresh job lands exactly the source rows from the start date on, overwriting or appending as its mode says.

Incremental sync
Incremental append adds only rows newer than the cursor, incremental dedup keeps the newest row per `id`, and the cursor advances to the largest committed `updated_at`.

Reconciled figures
Job counts, table row counts and the workspace figures are computed from stored rows and agree with each other.

Schema change policy
When a stream gains a field the next sync propagates it, ignores it or pauses the connection as its policy says, and reactivating a paused connection from its current version accepts the fields as they stand.

Job record
A finished job carries its attempts, per-stream counts, log, timings and the connection and connector versions it ran on, and the history lists jobs newest first.

Reset
Reset empties a connection's existing tables and clears its cursors, as qualified in Business rules.

One job at a time
A connection runs at most one job, so a second sync, a reset during a run and a sync of an inactive connection are refused with 409.

Simultaneous requests
Of simultaneous sync requests for one connection exactly one creates a job, and of simultaneous creations with one connection name exactly one creates a connection.

Idempotency
A replayed `Idempotency-Key` returns the first connection or job before the key expires, simultaneous replays create exactly one and answer with its id or as in flight, and reusing a live key with another body is refused.

Cancel and failure
A cancelled or failed job changes no table and no cursor, and rejected credentials fail after three attempts.

Live job events
The job event stream sends each log line and the final status to a holder of a valid session token.

Sync on the connection page
"Sync now", "Cancel", "Reset" and the "Connection active" switch work from the connection page, with each job result shown in the history and announced.

Flow diagram motion
The flow diagram moves while a job runs and is still when idle or under reduced motion.

Sync sounds
With "Sync sounds" on, a finished job plays a chime whose notes are Web Audio oscillators started in the page, and with it off no audio node starts.

Job history paging
Job history pages newest first with an opaque cursor bound to its listing, returns each earlier job exactly once while new jobs start, and refuses a page size outside 1 to 100 or a foreign or altered cursor.

Warehouse records
Warehouse records page forward and back in written order with `total_count` and a cursor bound to their table and its current generation, and the table page shows 50 rows at a time.

Sandbox API
The sandbox invoices API requires its key and pages the seven invoices.

Builder test read
A Builder test read follows every page and detects field types, a refused key is reported as a source error, and the manifest is validated.

Sandbox-only reads
A Builder base address or stream path that, once decoded and resolved, leaves `/mock-api/` is refused before anything is read.

Published connectors
Publishing creates a versioned custom source definition whose sources sync their streams with the version current when each job is created.

Builder page
The Builder's "UI" and "YAML" tabs stay in step and its "Test" button lists the records read.

Preferences
Each user's sync sounds and theme persist across sessions, and the dark theme darkens the console.

Command palette
Control+K or Command+K opens the command palette, which opens a matching connection and returns focus on Escape.

Console accessibility
Console pages meet WCAG 2.2 AA in both themes and show a visible focus indicator on every control reached by Tab.

Console touch targets
At 375 CSS pixels wide every console control and navigation link is at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels.

Console reduced motion
Under reduced motion no console loop runs and no content is lost.

Home page
The home page shows its headline, actions and architecture story, with its decorative drawing surface hidden from assistive technology.

Home motion
The hero backdrop shimmers, the architecture lines draw with the scroll, sections fade up and metrics count up, and under reduced motion every loop, scroll effect and count-up stops with content kept in place.

Film
The film with its captions and chapters is served, plays muted on its own only without reduced motion, and seeks by chapter.

Consent and privacy
No analytics identifier is stored, and a dismissed consent card stays hidden.

Marketing routes
Each marketing route loads with its headline without waiting for scripts, and an unknown address answers 404 with a link home.

Marketing chrome
The header, menus and footer are the same on every marketing route, the menus work by keyboard and pointer, and the filled primary action darkens on hover.

Pricing page
The pricing page shows four plan cards and the plan comparison, one plan at a time behind a "Plan" switch below 768 CSS pixels, and the credit package changes the Team price.

Responsive public layout
Public pages reflow from 320 CSS pixels with no sideways scrolling, stack on phones, fold the header into a menu and show three catalog columns from 992 CSS pixels.

Public accessibility
Public pages meet WCAG 2.2 AA, show visible focus on every control reached by Tab and meet the touch target size.

Visual system
The public site and console follow the colour, type, shape and status language described in Visual design.

Component architecture
Shared pieces are built once as reusable components that look and behave the same wherever they appear.

Interrupted jobs recover
A job left pending or running when the server stops is failed as interrupted on the next start, before health answers 200, and the connection can sync again.

Role changes take effect at once
A role change applies to every existing session of the member on its very next request.

Safe return after sign-in
A signed-out console address sends the person to `/login` with a `next` address, and sign-in returns them there only when it resolves inside `/app`, otherwise to `/app`.

Connection versions
A connection carries a version raised by one on each change listed in Business rules, and a PATCH needs a current `If-Match`, answering 428 without one and 412 `version_mismatch` when stale, so exactly one of simultaneous PATCHes from one version succeeds.

Jobs keep their starting versions
A job runs on the connection settings and connector manifest of the versions it recorded at creation and on the source records as they stood when it began running, and changes made after those moments apply from the next job.

Records page address
The warehouse table page keeps its page in the address, so reload, a shared link, Back and Forward show the same rows, and a stale or foreign page link shows the no-longer-valid alert.

Marketing keyboard model
The story tabs, the phone "Plan" switch, the header menus and the narrow "Menu" overlay work fully by keyboard as described in Interactions.

Invitation expiry
An invitation accepted at or after the end of its configured lifetime is refused with 410 `invite_expired`, stores nothing, and no longer blocks a new invitation to that email.

Honest role select
A refused role change returns the "Role for <member name>" select to the role the server holds and announces why.

Unknown fields refused
Every JSON body accepts only the fields its API entry lists, at every depth, and any other key answers 400 `validation` naming its dotted path with nothing stored.

Console retries reuse their key
The console sends an `Idempotency-Key` with "Create connection" and "Sync now", resends the same key after a lost or 5xx answer, sends a fresh key after an answered request or a wizard change, and shows a replay as success.

All-or-nothing visibility
Every reader sees a sync's tables, records, cursors, job and workspace figures either all before its commit or all after it, and a job's rows only once it reads Succeeded.

Reset leaves no trace
A reset empties the connection's existing tables and invalidates their page links, creates no table, keeps the status, version, known schema and job history, and equals one serial order when it meets a sync.

Named history and records tables
The Job history and warehouse records tables carry the published names, columns and row headers, and "Load older jobs" merges pages by job id so every job shows exactly once while new jobs arrive.

Seed identity
The seed creates each seeded row once under a fixed seed identity, and a restart never re-creates, renames, re-plans, re-roles or re-versions a seeded row someone has changed, as qualified in Seed data.

Published surface only
No generated documentation, schema, trailing-slash redirect or unpublished method answers, and a defined `/api` path called with another method answers 405 `method_not_allowed` with an `Allow` header naming its published methods.

Literal, bounded input
Catalog search matches its text literally within 100 characters, and a request string carrying a NUL, a value of the wrong JSON type or a body that is not a JSON object is refused with 400 `validation` naming its field, never 422 or a 5xx.

Key lifetime
An `Idempotency-Key` answers as a replay only before its `expires_at`, and at or after it the same key is a new request that runs every check and, on success, is recorded again.

Honest connection switch
A refused "Connection active" toggle leaves the page showing the stored connection's status, name, schedule and next run, announces why, and the next toggle carries the stored version.

Object checks on every route
Every job, log, event, cancel, tables and records route answers 404 `not_found` for an object of another workspace, a malformed id or a table name that is not a listed table of that destination, and never touches that object.

Readable plan comparison
The plan comparison is a table named "Compare the plans" whose every cell states its value in words, with glyphs hidden from assistive technology and AA contrast, at every width.

Database outage copy
When the database cannot be reached every page route, the media and the not-found page still answer from the server, and an action answered 503 `service_unavailable` shows the published database outage copy in `alert` with the form values kept.

Published landing routes
A signed-in person opening `/login` lands on `/app`, a console page the current role may not open is replaced by `/app` with the permission alert, the palette offers only allowed pages, and an unknown, foreign or malformed connection or table address shows its published not-found view.

Wizard draft survives sign-in
When "Create connection" answers 401 the wizard draft is kept in that tab for the same user and restored once, on its saved step with every value, after that user signs in again, and it is discarded for anyone else.

Live Streams table
The connection page's "Streams" table shows each selected stream's sync mode, row count and cursor, and at a job's end its Rows and Cursor cells change in the same render as the job row and the "Sync status" copy.

Dialog and paging survive refreshes
The job history refresh, job events and job ends never close, re-mount or move focus out of an open "Reset connection" dialog, and never drop the focus on "Load older jobs" or the older rows already loaded.

Console breakpoints
The console shows the "Navigation" drawer below 992 CSS pixels and the "Console" rail from 992, places the job history beside the live log from 1280, and scrolls records sideways inside a focusable frame with a pinned row header.

Closed panels are unavailable
A closed header menu, the closed "Menu" overlay, the closed "Navigation" drawer and a dismissed consent card are out of the accessibility tree and the Tab order, and widening past 992 CSS pixels with an overlay open closes it and leaves nothing inert.

Latest catalog input wins
The catalog's cards, "Showing N" count and address always match the latest controls, discarding any earlier answer that arrives late.

Announced sync progress
"Sync status" announces "Starting sync…", "Sync running" and the final copy once each in that order, and the live log shows every line exactly once across reconnects by the published event ids.

Next run in its zone
The dashboard and the connection page show each next run in the published format, in the connection's own time zone with its UTC offset.

Unreadable YAML holds the tab
While "Manifest YAML" cannot be read the YAML tab stays selected, the published copy describes the field, and "Test" and "Publish" are disabled.

Event streams release the database
An open job event stream holds no database connection of its own while it waits, stops its work within 5 seconds of its client leaving, and fifty open streams never slow other requests past one second.
`/app/run.json` holds string `install` and `build` commands, a nonempty `serve` command, and `"_schema":"run-manifest-v1"`.
Python dependencies install into `/app/.venv`, and `run.json` calls Python tools only as `.venv/bin/<tool>` or as `python -m <tool>` with that venv, with no global or `sudo` installs.
`/app/USER_README.md` lists every seeded Lumen Freight login and the seeded password.
The reserved directories `.browser_screenshots/` and `.downloads/` exist at the app root and are empty.

`/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` names every shipped package with its licence, plus the film and the three font families. "Shipped packages" means the production dependency tree: `npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`, plus every package in the Python requirements installed into `.venv`.
Every shipped package is under MIT, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, ISC, 0BSD or PSF-2.0. The fonts are under OFL-1.1, and the film is in the public domain.
The app uses no datastore except the provided PostgreSQL: no SQLite or other database file, no Redis, and no state files outside the database.
The shipped film file is byte-identical to the one stated in Deployment.
